sections.text:
After the destruction of the people of Aad, another tribe called Thamud appeared, and lived in the Al-Hijr region between the Hijaz and the Levant.

God gave them many blessings, just as He gave Ad. They enjoyed fertile lands, orchards, and wonderful agricultural springs.

The people of Thamud were distinguished by their exceptional skill in construction and architecture. They used to carve luxurious houses from the high mountains as if they were palaces.

They used to make summer palaces on the plains, and in the winter they would take refuge in their houses carved into the rock to protect them from the cold and storms.

But, unfortunately, they followed the same path as those who preceded them. They became arrogant with their skill and arrogance, and they worshiped idols and forgot the blessings.

God sent them a prophet from among them, and he was Saleh, peace be upon him. He was an honorable man, known among them for his clear mind and wisdom since his childhood.

Salih began to invite them kindly: “O my people, worship God. You have no god but Him. He produced you from the earth and settled you therein.”

He reminded them of God’s blessings upon them, and warned them of the fate of the people of Aad, which was not far from them.

But the elders and leaders denounced his call, and said to him: “O Saleh, you were hoped for by us before this,” meaning we were hoping that you would be our leader, so how do you call us to leave the gods of our fathers?
Not only did they reject his call, but they challenged him and demanded a tangible, physical miracle to prove that he was a messenger from God.

They pointed to a large, solid rock in the mountain, and said to him: “If you are truthful, then bring out for us from this rock a (pregnant) she-camel, tall and great, with specific, impossible specifications!”

Saleh agreed after taking covenants and covenants from them that they would believe if God fulfilled their request.

Saleh called upon his Lord and pleaded with Him, and God responded to him, so that the miracle would be a proof against them.

The solid rock split before their astonished eyes, and from it emerged a great and beautiful she-camel with exactly the specifications they had requested!
The she-camel was a dazzling divine miracle (“God’s she-camel”), a clear and undeniable sign. Some people believed, but the majority continued in their disbelief and stubbornness.

Saleh ordered his people to let the camel eat from God’s earth and not harm it, because any harm done to it would bring them imminent torment.

The camel was so huge that it drank all the water from the well one day, and left it for the people the next day, and on the day it drank it, it produced enough milk for all the people of the village!
They lived like this for a while, but hatred and hatred began to penetrate the hearts of the unbelievers who hated the presence of the Ayatollah among them.

Nine miscreants gathered in the city and decided on a diabolical plan: to get rid of the camel and kill it!
One night, they were lurking for the camel, and their brother, named Qaddar bin Salif, shot her with an arrow, then pounced on her and mauled her with a sword until she died.

They were not satisfied with that, but they challenged Salih and said insolently: “O Salih, bring us what you promise us if you are one of the messengers.”

Saleh felt deep sadness for killing the camel and daring to incite God’s wrath, and he told them that torment would befall them after only three days.

He said to them: “Enjoy yourselves in your home for three days. This is a promise that will not be lied to.”

On the first day, their faces turned yellow with fear and terror.

On the second day, their faces turned red.

On the third day, their faces turned black with despair and panic.

On the morning of the fourth day, the awaited torment came.

God sent upon them a loud and terrifying cry from heaven, and a violent tremor that shook the ground beneath their feet.

Their hearts broke in their chests from the horror of the sound, and they all died in their fortified homes that they had carved into the mountains, thinking that they would protect them.

They became crouched in their homes, as if they had never sung there nor lived a single day of bliss.

God saved Saleh and those who believed with him and they left the place, leaving behind a destroyed city to be a sign for those behind them.

The great lesson from this story is that force and physical fortifications, no matter how precise, do not repel God’s might.

And disbelief in blessings and persistence in corruption and killing of God’s signs is the shortest path to the destruction of nations.
